challenges.title: The chai stall's week
challenges.story: Ravi runs a chai stall outside a college. He wrote down how many cups he sold each day. The price per cup sits in one cell, so if he raises it next month, every figure should update on its own.

tasks.prompt: In **C6:C12**, work out each day's revenue: cups × the price in **B3**. Lock the price so you can fill down.
hints: B3 must not move when you fill: make it $B$3 (press F4).

mistakes.msg: Monday is right but the other days aren't: B3 moved when you filled. Lock it as $B$3.

tasks.prompt: In **C13**, total the week's revenue.
hints: SUM does it in one go.

tasks.prompt: In **B14**, show the average cups sold per day.
In **B15**, show the most cups sold on any day.

challenges.explain: Revenue is cups × price, with the price locked as $B$3 so every row points at the same cell. Change B3 to 18 and the whole week updates. The total, average and best day are SUM, AVERAGE and MAX over the day rows.

challenges.title: A GST invoice that adds up
challenges.story: Sharma Stationers sends this invoice to a school. The GST rate is in G3. The school's accountant will check the arithmetic, so every amount must be a formula.

tasks.prompt: In **D4:D8**, work out each line's amount: Qty × Rate.
hints: Both cells move with the row, so no $ is needed.

tasks.prompt: In **D10**, the subtotal of the five amounts.
hints: Point at the cells; don't type numbers.

tasks.prompt: In **D11**, the GST: subtotal × the rate in **G3**.
hints: Point at G3 instead of typing 18%.

mistakes.msg: Point at G3 rather than typing the rate.
Point at G3 rather than typing the rate.

tasks.prompt: Show **D4:D12** as rupees with Indian grouping.
tasks.fmtMsg: Choose Rupees, Indian grouping, in the number-format box.

tasks.prompt: In **D12**, the total due: subtotal plus GST.

challenges.explain: Each line is =B4*C4, filled down. The subtotal is SUM(D4:D8), GST is =D10*G3 pointing at the rate cell, and the total is =D10+D11. A rupee format with Indian grouping makes 1,25,000.00 easy to read.

challenges.title: Who had the best season?
challenges.story: The club captain wants a season summary for three batters. Write each formula once for Ananya, then fill it across to Rohit and Kiran.

tasks.prompt: In **B12:D12**, total each player's runs. Write it in B12 and fill right.
hints: Drag the fill handle right to D12, or press Ctrl+R.
Each column gets its own total.

tasks.prompt: In **B13:D13**, each player's average.
In **B14:D14**, each player's highest score.
In **B15:D15**, each player's lowest score.
Who had the best season by total runs?

challenges.explain: Each summary row is written once in column B and filled right: the column letter moves from B to C to D, so each formula looks at its own player. Totals: Ananya 376, Rohit 347, Kiran 334.

challenges.title: Where does the money go?
challenges.story: A family wants to see which bills take the biggest share of their monthly spending, with the largest at the top.

tasks.prompt: In **B13**, total the bills.
In **C4:C11**, each bill's share of the total: amount ÷ the total in **B13**. Lock the total.

mistakes.msg: The first share is right, the rest aren't: the total's address moved. Lock it as $B$13.

tasks.prompt: Show the shares in **C4:C11** as percentages.
Sort the bills so the **largest amount** comes first (rows 4 to 11).

challenges.explain: Each share is the bill divided by the locked total, $B$13. Formatted as a percentage, the shares add up to 100%. Sorting by amount, largest first, puts Maid and Electricity at the top.

challenges.title: A payroll that follows the rates
challenges.story: HR keeps the HRA and PF rates in G1 and G2. When the rates change next year, nobody should have to edit a single formula.

tasks.prompt: In **C4:C8**, HRA = Basic × the HRA rate in **G1**.

mistakes.msg: Only the first row is right: lock the rate as $G$1.

tasks.prompt: In **D4:D8**, PF = Basic × the PF rate in **G2**.

mistakes.msg: Only the first row is right: lock the rate as $G$2.

tasks.prompt: In **E4:E8**, Net pay = Basic + HRA − PF.

challenges.explain: HRA and PF point at the rate cells with absolute references ($G$1, $G$2). Net pay uses relative references because every cell it needs is on the same row. Change a rate and the whole sheet follows.

challenges.title: Clean up the attendance list
challenges.story: The workshop sign-in sheet has gaps and a couple of hours typed as text, so the totals come out wrong. Tidy it so Excel can count properly.

tasks.prompt: Remove the **blank rows** inside the list (rows 3 to 12).
hints: Right-click a row number › Delete row.
Rows 6 and 9 (row 9 becomes 8 after the first).

tasks.prompt: After removing the gaps, Harsh's and Kavya's hours (now in **B6** and **B9**) are text. Make them real numbers: **5** and **6**.
hints: Text numbers sit on the left with a green triangle.
Click the cell and retype the number.

tasks.prompt: In **B11**, count how many people have hours recorded.

challenges.explain: Blank rows split a list, so remove them first. Hours typed as text ("5") are skipped by SUM and COUNT, so retype them as numbers. After that, =COUNT(B4:B10) gives 7.

challenges.title: Unit test report card
challenges.story: A teacher's mark sheet is half finished, and one formula shows #DIV/0!. Finish the totals and averages, then fix the error.

tasks.prompt: In **E3:E8**, each student's total across the three subjects.
hints: Each row adds its own marks.

tasks.prompt: In **B10:D10**, the class average for each subject.
**B13** shows #DIV/0!. Fix it so it gives the class's average total: the sum of E3:E8 ÷ the number of students in **B12**.
hints: Press F2 on B13: it divides by B14, which is empty.
The count of students is in B12.

mistakes.msg: Fix the cause rather than hiding the error with IFERROR.

challenges.explain: Totals fill down (each row has its own marks) and averages fill right (each column has its own subject). The #DIV/0! came from dividing by an empty cell; pointing at the count in B12 fixes it.

challenges.title: How far does a litre go?
challenges.story: Neha logs her scooter's odometer every time she fills up. She wants to know the distance between fills and how many kilometres she gets per litre.

tasks.prompt: In **D4:D8**, the distance since the last fill: this odometer reading minus the one above.
hints: Both references should move as you fill down.

tasks.prompt: In **E4:E8**, km per litre: distance ÷ litres filled.
In **E10**, the average km per litre.

challenges.explain: =B4-B3 looks at this row's reading and the one above; filled down, each row keeps that same shape. km per litre is distance ÷ litres, and the average is AVERAGE(E4:E8).
